- A set of acceptance tests we can run and sign off on
- An expected close timeline for evaluation -> production handoff so procurement can align budgets

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: acceptance scenario catalog + release triggers

C.,

Attached is a first-pass MAP and an "acceptance scenario catalog" that maps tests to concrete pass/fail thresholds (MAP-Acme-v0.1.xlsx). High-level summary below — please review and flag any adjustments.

High-level success criteria (pilot evaluation):
- Functional correctness: domain extraction F1 >= 0.87 on the provided 2k sample prompt set
- Safety/regression: no high-severity hallucination cases (>0) in sample audit; overall hallucination rate < 1.5%
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250 ms (single-turn; model trimmed for 512 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 35 qps during peak simulated workload with p95 latency target met
- Reliability: end-to-end availability >= 99.5% for the pilot window
- Cost sensitivity: per-1000-token unit economics within 15% of the forecast in the pricing sheet

Exit gates (hard blockers for pilot acceptance):
- Missing signed DPA or unresolved data residency requirement
- Security questionnaire items with "blocker" severity (items 1.2, 3.4) not closed or mitigated
- Inability to demonstrate KV/prefix cache behavior on your sample traffic that meets latency targets

Acceptance tests (what we'll run together):
1) Smoke suite — basic end-to-end flows: pass/fail, owner: Redwood Solutions (target: Apr 20)
2) Regression audit — sample of 500 flagged prompts compared against baseline (pass if <1.5% hallucination)
3) Load/stress — synthetic load to validate throughput at target qps (pass if p95 latency met)
4) Data retention & deletion test — confirm row-level deletion triggers within 24h
5) Security checklist verification — confirm SOC2 controls and KMS integration for keys used in pilot

Owners & deadlines (proposed):
- Redwood: provide test harness + acceptance-tests.yaml (owner: Karthik) — by Apr 9
- Acme: provide final sample dataset + procurement checklist (owner: C. Taylor) — by Apr 9
- Joint run of acceptance tests — Apr 20–23 (pilot smoke + regression)

Next steps:
- I attached the spreadsheet (MAP-Acme-v0.1.xlsx) and a YAML skeleton for the acceptance tests (we'll push to the shared Drive). Can you confirm you and Procurement are OK with the dates and thresholds by end of day Thu?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the criteria.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183
Attachments: MAP-Acme-v0.1.xlsx, acceptance-tests.yaml

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: acceptance scenario catalog + release triggers

Lauren / C.,

I reviewed the acceptance-tests.yaml skeleton. A few operational notes from infra:
- For the p95 latency we should prepare two profiles:
  * Optimistic (GPU-optimized, quantized fp16) target p95 <= 250 ms
  * Conservative (mixed-precision fallback) target p95 <= 320 ms
  We'll run both and log which profile passed.
- We can stand up a dedicated pool for the pilot (reserved nodes) — cost estimate in the spreadsheet is approximate; will confirm after we pick the quantized artifact.
- I'll own the test harness and put the runner + results in the Drive folder (acceptance-tests.yaml -> CI job that emits a JSON report).

Action items for Redwood:
- Karthik -> deliver test harness + runner by Apr 9
- Vivek -> prepare rollback runbook (if regression >2%) and a warm fallback model (owner: vivek_kulkarni) by Apr 16

C., if you need a looser latency SLO for the conservative profile we can accommodate — please call out which profile you prefer for sign-off.

-Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
